steps.name: Paired within-subject DE (DESeq2, subject blocked)
caveats: With 5 pairs the residual df is 4: dispersions and padj are low-powered; frame significance as preliminary and do not over-interpret genes near the threshold.
Genes with all-zero counts in one group are handled by DESeq2's internal filtering/NA pvalues — report how many, do not drop them manually.
Do not re-estimate normalization per subject; DESeq2's global size factors are correct for this contrast.
steps.context: Counts: /eval-four-models-v2-without-paired-n5-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv — raw integers from STAR/featureCounts, first column gene ID, then 10 sample columns (12,000 genes). Metadata: /eval-four-four-models-v2-without-paired-n5-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (10 rows; sample, subject, condition). Each of 5 subjects contributes exactly one control and one treated sample. R toolchain has DESeq2 1.52.0 and apeglm 1.34.0 installed; nothing is installed at run time.
steps.question: In the 5-subject paired blood RNA-seq design (one control and one treated sample per subject), which genes show a treatment effect after accounting for subject — i.e., the within-subject response?
constraints: Read the condition column of metadata.csv and identify its two values; designate the control value as the reference level. If the values are not clearly a control/treated pair, stop and report the actual values.
Verify the pairing before modeling: exactly 5 subjects, each with one control and one treated sample; abort with a clear message if any subject lacks a pair.
Use design ~ subject + condition (subject first) so the treatment coefficient is the within-subject contrast.
Filter out genes with total count < 10 across all 10 samples; report how many were removed and keep the filter deterministic.
Shrink log2FoldChange with apeglm; report the shrunken log2FoldChange alongside the unshrunken stat/pvalue/padj (BH, DESeq2 default).

Save as artifacts: the full DESeq2 object (RDS), the complete results table (all retained genes, sorted by pvalue), per-sample size factors, and QC outputs (per-sample library sizes, pairwise sample-sample correlations, MA plot).
steps.description: Build the DESeq2 model with subject as a fixed effect, test treatment on top of it, shrink LFCs with apeglm, and emit the full per-gene results table plus QC summaries and the saved object for downstream steps.
acceptance_criteria: Results table has one row per retained gene with baseMean, log2FoldChange (apeglm-shrunken), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj.
The fitted model matrix confirms the treatment coefficient is an estimable within-subject contrast (5 pairs; residual df = 4) and is reported as such.
Counts of genes with padj < 0.05 and padj < 0.1 are reported (an explicit zero is a valid outcome).
QC artifacts exist and any isolated sample (e.g., correlation < 0.9 with the others) is flagged in the summary.

steps.name: Per-subject within-pair response profile
caveats: The 0.25 log2FC threshold is arbitrary; report the 0.5 tier and do not present 0.25 as a biological boundary.
With n = 5 the one-sample t-test is sensitive to outliers and the Wilcoxon is nearly underpowered; present both and lean on concordance counts as the primary per-subject evidence.
A gene can be subject-specific (changed in 1-2 subjects) yet not significant in T1S1 — report that intersection explicitly rather than silently dropping it.
steps.context: Loads the DESeq2 object and results table saved by T1S1 from the same run — do not re-normalize or re-estimate anything. The per-subject view is what directly answers 'within each subject', complementing the population-level treatment test of T1S1.
steps.question: For each of the 5 subjects individually, which genes change in that subject's own control-to-treated comparison, and how many treatment-responsive genes change in the same direction in all 5 subjects?
constraints: Load the DESeq2 object saved by T1S1 and use its normalization for all within-pair log2FC computations.
For each subject: within-pair log2FC = log2(normalized treated) - log2(normalized control).
Define a per-subject response at |log2FC| >= 0.25; also compute at 0.5 and report both tiers side by side.

Per-gene concordance table: per-subject log2FC columns, counts of subjects with up (>= 0.25), down (<= -0.25), and no change; flag 'consistent responder' = padj < 0.05 in T1S1 AND same sign in all 5 subjects; flag 'subject-specific' = changed in <= 2 of 5 subjects.

Cross-check: per-gene one-sample t-test on the 5 within-pair log2FCs against 0, plus the Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value for comparison; report Spearman rank correlation of within-pair log2FC (per-gene mean) with the T1S1 shrunken LFC and the rank correlation of -log10 p-values between the two tests.
Save: per-subject top-20 gene tables, the per-gene concordance table, per-subject MA/volcano plots, and a concordance summary plot.
steps.description: Compute each subject's within-pair log2FC from the T1S1 normalization, build a per-gene concordance table (response counts, consistent-responder and subject-specific flags), cross-check with a model-free one-sample test, and produce per-subject gene tables and plots.
acceptance_criteria: Per-gene concordance table exists with per-subject log2FC columns, response counts, and the consistent/subject-specific flags.
The cross-check statistics (rank correlations of LFC and p-values between model-based and model-free tests) are reported as numbers, not just stated as done.
Per-subject tables and plots are saved as artifacts.

steps.name: Pathway context of responsive genes
caveats: With few or no padj < 0.05 genes (likely, given 4 residual df), the set-based tier is empty — present only the ranked-list fgsea result and label it suggestive.
WikiPathways covers pathways unevenly; a negative result is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
steps.context: Input: the T1S1 results table (shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, padj). Reference: the human WikiPathways GMT provisioned under /mnt/refs (HGNC symbols, one set per line, first field '%'-delimited name/ID/species) — resolve it against the reference store at run time; organism matches the dataset (Homo sapiens). fgsea 1.38.0 and org.Hs.eg.db 3.23.1 are installed. No network access: do not call KEGG REST or any external API.
steps.question: Which human pathways are represented among the treatment-responsive genes, to annotate the gene list from T1S1/T1S2?
constraints: Map the results-table gene IDs to HGNC symbols with org.Hs.eg.db (skip if already symbols); report the mapping rate and exclude unmapped genes.
Rank genes by stat (signed, descending) and run fgsea against the human WikiPathways GMT.
If the T1S1 padj < 0.05 set is non-empty, additionally report how many of those genes fall into the top 20 fgsea pathways (simple membership counts, no network-based enrichment).
If the human WikiPathways GMT is absent from the reference store at run time, report the gap and finish the step with a note that pathway context is unavailable — do not substitute a non-human GMT.
steps.description: Run fgsea on the full T1S1 ranked list against the human WikiPathways GMT (organism-matched: Homo sapiens, HGNC symbols), and summarize pathway membership of the padj < 0.05 genes if that set is non-empty. Annotation only — the gene list is the deliverable.
acceptance_criteria: Top-20 pathway table with set, NES, pvalue, and padj is saved.
The mapping rate, the size of the gene set used, and the empty/non-empty status of the significant-gene tier are reported.
Ranked-list results are labeled as directional/suggestive where the significant-gene tier is empty.

plan.title: Paired within-subject treatment DE, human blood
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are a 5-subject paired bulk RNA-seq design in human blood: 12,000 genes x 10 samples of STAR/featureCounts raw integers, with one control and one treated sample per subject. Because the question asks what responds within each subject, subject is treated as a fixed blocking effect and treatment is tested on top of it (T1S1, DESeq2 with apeglm LFC shrinkage) — this is the standard paired-design contrast, and with 5 pairs it carries only 4 residual degrees of freedom, which must be reported as a power caveat. T1S2 computes each subject's own within-pair log2FC from the same normalization to answer which genes respond in each subject and how consistently direction is conserved across subjects, cross-checked against a model-free one-sample test. T1S3 adds organism-matched pathway context (human WikiPathways, present in the reference store, via fgsea on the ranked list) as annotation only — it is not part of the gene-list deliverable.
